svg.title: Now insert, at each separated atlas copy, the negative terminal reference observable, transport its marked polynomial exactly from N to k, and multiply there by the corresponding coarse lens insertion. Equation (AP6) identifies the resulting first marked slot and forced slot with the residual- history slots. The paid insertion transport theorem then carries those slots from k down to m, along the same migrating copy positions. The separation and occupancy bounds are obtained from the chosen atlas at each intermediate scale. The resulting insertion at m has the served-source bound with support exponent of that scale and the two vault bounds 2, 1 used in the root extraction. The residual-history estimates pay both bounds; no new history or mark schedule is chosen during this transport.
